notes: The portable design puts the number on the largest visible panel per side,
which on a 500 is the rear quarter. That is a defensible guess and the wrong
one: the shape has a big flat door and a rear quarter that curves away over
the arch, so the number goes on the door where a touring car would wear it.
The doors are laid sideways in this texture — 270 degrees on the left, 90
on the right — so the design's rects, which put the name beside the number
along a sidepod, put it in a box 138 mm long here and shrank it to 15 mm
letters. The number and team name below are find_space's layout for the
left door, number over name, which measures 287 mm and 107 mm letters;
the right side is the same, mirrored the way this car flips it.
The driver name is dropped. The door holds two lines at a size that reads
from trackside, and a 500 has nowhere else good to put a third: the panel
above the door is 2.3% of the texture at 1.28 anisotropy, a sliver,
stretched. Saying so is better than shrinking it until it is unreadable.
The team names name their panel, the door, although the design's own
selection finds it today. Regenerated with extents, the rear quarter also
reaches the middle of the car and is the bigger match, and the name would
have moved onto it with this fit's placement.
